templates.description: Direct diplomatic, trade, or military tension transmission from flashpoint shocks into allied posture and market risk premia.
Maritime chokepoint closure or export controls constrain physical throughput initially before alternative legal energy supply routes buffer the impact.
Reciprocal mobilization crosses adversary redlines when diplomatic off-ramps fall silent, triggering rapid conflict escalation.
Prolonged disruption to cross-border trade reduces the availability of staple goods and medical supplies.
Rising fiscal strain, casualties, and home-front protest reduce political leaders' tolerance for sustained expeditionary escalation.
